name: metabolism-biomass-yield-s1b-anaerobic-contrast
title: Does the model's own aerobic-to-anaerobic yield drop match biology?
question: Real E. coli anaerobic biomass yield is several-fold below aerobic, because without a terminal electron acceptor the cell cannot extract ATP by respiration. A model that barely respires aerobically (O2:glucose ~0.09, RQ ~3.6) has little respiratory contribution to lose, so it should show a much smaller drop. Does it? This is a first-principles discriminator that needs no external reference data - the model is compared against its own aerobic result.

assumptions.text: A minimal_minus_oxygen run is comparable to the aerobic baseline on yield once each is measured with the same estimator over the same burn-in window, so the ratio between them isolates the respiratory contribution.

tests.name: anaerobic-yield-drop-matches-respiratory-contribution
tests.question: Is the aerobic-to-anaerobic yield ratio several-fold, as in real E. coli, or close to 1 as a barely-respiring model would predict?

measure.detail: Yxs by direct mass balance under minimal_minus_oxygen, divided by the aerobic Yxs from metabolism-biomass-yield-s1-diagnostic measured the same way.
